thread:
marta: Quick idea — instead of static weights for canaries, what if we do latency-aware adaptive weighting? shift traffic down from a cohort when p95 > threshold, slowly ramp back when healthy. low-risk and automatic. :thinking_face:

alex: Interesting. how do you avoid oscillation if metric noise spikes?

priya: we could add a cooldown and step-size limit + require min sample count before flip. also tie to quota checks so we don't accidentally blast stable when dedicated capacity is hit.

marta: exactly. sketch of config I had in mind: ```
route: /generate
cohort: new-transform-v2
initial_weight: 0.05
max_step: 0.10   # max change per eval
p95_threshold_ms: 280
min_samples: 200
cooldown_seconds: 300
fallback_route: stable
metrics_window: 5m
```

dan: we'd need the console to show current weight, last change reason, and the p95 time series for that cohort. UX idea: inline traffic slider + auto-mode badge (on/off) so SREs can nudge. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: what about correlated failures — e.g., one region sees latency spike but others fine. policy should be region-aware and maybe consider origin header. also sticky session users shouldn't get bounced around mid-request.

marta: agree. plan is: cohort predicates can include region or header, and we do per-cohort kv for sticky sessions when applicable. if request has session cookie we honor stickiness first, then routing policy.

priya: name collision concern: teams might make lots of adaptive cohorts and forget to clean them up. add TTL or tags + console filter. also quota accounting on a per-cohort basis so billing + SLA match.

marta: good ops constraints. also want a safety guard: if fallback route returns >5% error rate in last 2m, pause all automatic shifts and page oncall.

deploy-bot: experiment.create job=adaptive-weighting-1893456789 user=marta status=queued

dan: telemetry-wise, we need a new rollup: per-cohort {requests, p50,p95,errors,avg_cost,weight} emitted every 30s. will add to the ingestion plan.

alex: small nit — we should make the step unit relative (percentage points) vs multiplicative so small weights don't jump to 0.2 instantly. think absolute_pct_step works.

marta: noted. action items: 1) infra: add eval loop + metrics emit (dan) 2) platform API: policy def + console UX (priya) 3) SRE: define paging thresholds + runbook (alex) 4) me: author RFC w/ config examples and safety tests. I'll ping next week. :v:

priya: sounds good. can you include a sample fallback policy for quota exhaustion? we had one customer who hit reserved cap and routing flipped unexpectedly.

marta: will add. sample fallback: `if quota_exhausted -> route: limited-capacity; notify: team`

alex: +1. also add an opt-out API for customers who prefer manual only.

marta: will include opt-out and a console toggle. thanks all — will draft RFC and drop in #eng-arch for review. :eyes:
